# TASKS

The queue. Pick by RUN.md §4. Status: `todo` / `in_progress` / `done` / `blocked`. A task counts as done only once STATE, TASKS and LOG are updated (RUN.md §6.5).

**Standard checks** (Node 24: `export PATH=/opt/homebrew/opt/node@24/bin:$PATH`):
- **ts-js:** `cd labs/ts-js && npm test` exits 0 (typecheck + vitest).
- **angular:** `cd labs/angular && npx ng build ui-lib` first (since HOUSE-40: `tsconfig.json` `paths` maps `ui-lib` to `dist/ui-lib`, which `tsc -p tsconfig.spec.json` and `ng test` need), then `npx ng build` and `npx ng test --watch=false` exit 0.
- **links gate:** until HOUSE-01 is done: `node labs/tools/check-links.mjs` reports **0 `missing anchor`** and every `missing file` target is a planned file (a SYLLABUS §1 module slug, or GLOSSARY / QUESTION-INDEX / CHEATSHEET / MOCK-INTERVIEWS / README). After HOUSE-01: `node labs/tools/check-links.mjs --planned` exits 0.

### Module 11 tasks (PLAN-M11) · common rules
- Inputs for every task: `_meta/modules/M11.md` (its section, question or exercise rows, the budget, "Lab decision", "Facts established while planning", "Could not be read", the owner map), STYLE-GUIDE §3-§8, QUALITY-BAR B-E, SYLLABUS §4 (11), the module skeleton, and the "Proposed FIX tasks" of REVIEW-M05..M09 (the lessons below come from them). Re-verify every fact the task uses before writing (lab > package source > official docs/specification) and record the basis next to the claim; everything under "Not yet read" for the task's section in M11.md must be read first or dropped.
- **REVIEW-M10 is still pending.** Before CLOSE-M11 (and, if it has landed, before each task), read `_meta/reviews/REVIEW-M10.md` if it exists and apply to module 11 every finding that recurs here (diagrams, cause clauses, first-use definitions, question links, "in the lab" claims, status markers, prose over budget). CLOSE-M11 records in its LOG line which REVIEW-M10 findings it applied, or that the file did not exist.
- **No real browser, no accessibility tree, no screen reader.** What a browser or an assistive technology does (accessibility tree, role mapping, announcements, native Tab order, `<dialog>` and `inert` behavior, `:focus-visible`, rendered contrast) is taught from cited specifications, MDN, the APG and web.dev, never as a lab observation. jsdom 30.1.1 is worded "in jsdom" and runs only what M11.md lists as working; the `Section 2: jsdom ...` pin tests record what it does not do (`showModal`, `inert`, rendering-aware `focus()`, sequential navigation, `computedRole`). Lab tests assert DOM state, never what a screen reader says. axe-core is a throwaway probe (observed on a date, scratch files deleted), never a committed test; `@angular/cdk` and `@angular/aria` are read from `npm pack` typings and are not installed; `labs/angular` is untouched.
- **Legal and standards claims** (WCAG 2.2 levels and criteria, the European Accessibility Act, its dates, scope and exemptions, EN 301 549) are written only from primary text read in the task (W3C, EUR-Lex or the Official Journal, the Commission). EUR-Lex returned an empty WAF challenge to curl and WebFetch on 2026-10-07: SEC-M11-01 tries other routes and otherwise uses the fallback in M11.md "Could not be read" and the Q11.02 fallback in the question list. SYLLABUS says "verified": record in the LOG line exactly which sentences are verified and from which page.
- **First-time-pass rules (recurring REVIEW findings; check each before marking done):**
  - Diagram: every section's Mental model has a Mermaid diagram (type named in M11.md) followed by a line starting `What to notice` (REVIEW-M05 T-2, M06 T-1, M07 T-1, M08 T-1, M09).
  - Misconceptions: every bullet gives the correction **and why the myth exists**; a "Once true: ... until ..." clause only from a source actually read in this task (cite or marker); otherwise only the cause. Never from memory (REVIEW-M05 T-4, M06 T-2, M07 T-3, M08 T-2, M09 T-1/T-2).
  - Status markers only in STYLE-GUIDE §3.2 forms at first mention (including any Angular, CDK or `@angular/aria` API); **Baseline is defined once** (SEC-M11-02's verification paragraph, MDN's wording) and never used as a stand-alone marker form; no Baseline or version claim unless the page was read in the task. ECMAScript edition at first mention for post-ES2015 features in TS snippets and exercise code (REVIEW-M08 T-4, M09 T-4).
  - Every term is defined on first use in this module (the per-section term list is in M11.md) with a link to the owning module; acronyms are expanded once (WCAG, ARIA, APG, AT, SC, EAA, POUR, SPA, NVDA, JAWS, VO, DOM, CSS...) (REVIEW-M05 T-6, M06 T-6, M07 T-6, M08 T-5, M09 T-2).
  - Questions: each is linked from its section body with its own `[Q11.NN](#q11-NN)` (never only range endpoints), and each answer links back to its section; exercises are linked from their sections (REVIEW-M08 T-7). Forward links before the anchor exists use plain text plus `<!-- relink: #q11-NN -->` / `<!-- relink: #ex11-N -->`; each QB/EX task turns its own back into links and deletes the comments; CLOSE: `grep -c "relink:"` is 0 (the Labs line's relink comment is turned into links by CLOSE-M11).
  - No "mutation check" or "checked by hand" claim; every claim of the form "in the lab, X" names a test (`Section N: ...`, `Q11.NN ...`, `E11.N ...`) that exists and asserts it exactly (REVIEW-M06 T-8, M08 T-6, M09 T-5).
  - Callouts begin with the `> [!NOTE]` / `> [!TIP]` line; no *Coming from the backend* callout is required in this module (REVIEW-M08 T-8).
  - Output questions only where a jsdom or lab-model test asserts the answer exactly (Q11.08, Q11.14, Q11.15); the answer states what jsdom or the model computes, never what a browser or a screen reader does.
  - Exercise statements and tests: Constraints list what the model does not cover; only behaviors the tests assert are stated as criteria; the exercise says it is a model of a specification (REVIEW-M09 T-5).
  - HTML, ARIA and CSS blocks start with a first-line comment (`<!-- Illustrative, not run -->`, `/* Illustrative, not run */` or `<!-- Run in jsdom: <test name> -->`); TS snippets are Complete, Excerpt or Partial per STYLE-GUIDE §7.2.
  - Prose budget: **the per-part budgets in M11.md are realistic and sum to about 9,400**; M10 sections ran 18% over, its bank 8%. Each task measures its part with `node labs/tools/module-stats.mjs` (and the QUALITY-BAR python one-liner), puts the count in its LOG line, and **cuts before finishing if more than 5% over its budget**, by removing repeats and never a diagram, a trap's cause or a "because". The module must stay at most 10,000 by `module-stats.mjs` after every task and 600 words are reserved for REVIEW fixes (a FIX that adds prose cuts at least as much).
  - Do not repeat what another module owns (M11.md owner map): events and `focusin` are 08, shadow DOM and `ElementInternals` are 08 §5, units, `order`, `color-scheme` and the top layer are 10, Angular host element semantics and ARIA bindings are 13, focus on navigation and titles are 24, error display strategies are 25 and 26, Testing Library is 29, axe in Playwright is 30, `lang` and RTL are 34, reduced-motion animation is 35, CDK a11y and Angular Aria are 36; use one sentence plus a link.
- Module file: replace only the task's own `<!-- TASK: <ID> ... -->` line, at the end of the task, in a single edit. Regions without their own marker (the verification paragraph placeholder, Short on time, Summary, Check your understanding, Connections) are the `<!-- PLACEHOLDER: ... -->` line, replaced by the task named in it. Never touch another task's marker.
- Labs: `labs/ts-js/src/modules/11-accessibility/` and `labs/ts-js/src/outputs/11-accessibility/` as listed in M11.md "Lab files". Tests that need a DOM start with `// @vitest-environment jsdom` and use `support/dom.ts` (**built once by SEC-M11-02 and read-only afterwards**; a task that needs a change records it and stops rather than editing it). No test needs the internet; no `any`.
- Every task adds its sources under `## Module 11 · Accessibility` in `SOURCES.md` (create it after the Module 10 section if absent) and its inline-defined terms under `## Module 11` in `_meta/GLOSSARY-TERMS.md`.

- **Angular code** follows STYLE-GUIDE §7.1 (standalone, `inject()`, signals, signal inputs/outputs, built-in control flow, no `changeDetection` property unless the example is about it, v22 file names, `protected`/`readonly` per the style guide, no `any`). Specs change signals, never plain fields (M13.md F45); fixtures that need a selector to match are nested in a host component's template (F44); selectors and templates are unique per fixture.
- **First-time-pass rules:** every section has a Mermaid diagram of the type named in M13.md followed by a line starting `What to notice` (quote labels with brackets, colons or `@`); **every** Misconceptions bullet gives the correction and a cause clause, and "Once true: … until …" only from a source read in the task; status markers only in the STYLE-GUIDE §3.2 forms at first mention with the version from a tag or the CHANGELOG; ECMAScript edition at first mention for post-ES2015 syntax; every term defined on first use with a link to the owner; questions linked from their section with their own `[Q13.NN](#q13-NN)` and answers link back; forward links before the anchor exists are plain text plus `<!-- relink: #q13-NN -->` / `<!-- relink: #ex13-N -->`, turned into links by the EX/QB task that creates the target; no "checked by hand" claim, every "in the lab, X" names a test (`Section N: …`, `Q13.NN …`, `E13.N …`) asserting exactly X; callouts begin `> [!NOTE]`/`> [!TIP]`, *Framework vs platform* callouts named in M13.md are required, every *Coming from the backend* callout states **Where the analogy breaks**; Output questions only where a spec asserts the answer exactly (Q13.05, Q13.06, Q13.07, Q13.11, Q13.13, Q13.15, Q13.22, Q13.28); compile-time answers quote dated `ngc` runs and are not tagged Output; exercise Constraints list what is not covered and only asserted behaviors are criteria; the two ts-js exercises say they are models (of the expression subset, of Angular's `ShadowCss`), not Angular's parser or compiler.
- **Prose budget** (Part D: pilot depth, no filler; the 10,000 cap does not apply): per-part budgets in M13.md sum to 18,540. Each task measures its part and the whole module with `node labs/tools/module-stats.mjs` and the QUALITY-BAR python one-liner (the tool does not flag Part D), puts both counts in its LOG line, and cuts before finishing if more than 5% over its budget. Answer parts average at most 230 words per QB chunk, none above 300; exercises about 580, at most 620.

- Module file: replace only the task's own `<!-- TASK: <ID> -->` line, at the end of the task, in a single edit. `<!-- PLACEHOLDER: … -->` lines are replaced by the task named in them. Never touch another task's marker. Labs: only the files M13.md "Lab files" assigns to the task, under `src/app/modules/13-components-and-templates/` (`labs/angular`) and `src/modules/13-components-and-templates/` (`labs/ts-js`).   - Factual slips: "which views refresh", "before versus after" and "first versus last" statements are checked against the recorded runs (F1-F21) before writing; every number in prose is traced to a test, run or read.

  - Factual slips: "which value", "at which frame", "first versus last", "before versus after complete" and "how many subscriptions" statements are checked against the recorded runs (F1-F33) before writing; every number in prose is traced to a test, run or read. **Do not repeat REVIEW-M22 F-1:** counting producer runs tells unicast from multicast, not cold from hot (link 22 §3 for the definitions). **F-2:** quote combinator and operator semantics with their exact completion and error rules (`race` follows the first notification, an error included; `concat` waits for completion).
  - Wording of observation (REVIEW-M22 F-4, T-6; REVIEW-M21): every "in the lab, X" names a test (`Section N: …`, `Q23.NN …`, `E23.N …`) asserting exactly X; no "not run" for something a test now asserts; no unrecorded run ("the run hung", "it crashed"); no unmeasured comparison ("less code", "twice as fast", "uses more memory"); a measured comparison names the count.
  - Quotes (REVIEW-M21): a quoted sentence is verbatim from the named file, branch and date; a shortened runtime message carries "(abridged)"; an error name or code is the one the source or the run gives, attributed to that source, not to the docs; a default is attached to the symbol that declares it (`refCount` is `shareReplay`'s, `resetOnRefCountZero` is `share`'s).
  - Header and history (REVIEW-M22 F-3, T-7; REVIEW-M21): the header lists only what the module teaches and cites; no RxJS 9 line; history sentences are dated from the CHANGELOG or typings only.
  - Markers (REVIEW-M21 C4): the marker sits at the **first body mention in the module**, not in a later section or in the question bank; a glossary entry never dates a deprecation the sources do not date (REVIEW-M22 F-7).
  - Owner credit (REVIEW-M22 F-8): name the owning module correctly in every link sentence (the `takeUntilDestroyed` mechanism is 20's, the strategy comparison 23's; flattening operators are 23's; `share()` defaults 22's; `toSignal` basics 17's).

  - Terms (REVIEW-M22 T-3, REVIEW-M21 B9): define at first use with an owner link (M23.md lists the terms per section); run a first-use script over the module before finishing.

- Inputs for every task: `_meta/modules/M24.md` (its section, question or exercise rows, the budget, "Lab decision", "Facts established while planning" F1-F34, "Could not be read" C1-C13, the owner map), STYLE-GUIDE §3-§8, QUALITY-BAR B-E, SYLLABUS §4 (24), the module skeleton, the pilot `modules/17-signals.md` and the finished `modules/22-rxjs-foundations.md` and `modules/23-rxjs-in-depth.md` for Part D depth (read a section, answer or exercise of the same kind before writing; never copy), and `_meta/reviews/REVIEW-M23.md` and `REVIEW-M22.md` § Findings and § Proposed FIX tasks. The facts of M24.md were probed 2026-10-10 on Angular 22.2.1 (`@angular/router` 22.2.1, `rxjs` 7.8.2, Node 24.21.0, jsdom 30.1.1) under `ng test` in a scratch copy of `labs/angular`; a task re-runs the ones it quotes under `ng test`. - **What runs and what is documented** (M24.md "Lab decision"): **every runtime claim is asserted by specs in `labs/angular` under `ng test`** (jsdom; `RouterTestingHarness` from `@angular/router/testing`; `TestBed.inject(ApplicationRef).bootstrap(Root, el)` for preloading and in-memory scrolling, which the harness does not start (F27); a `document.startViewTransition` stub for view transitions, deleted in `finally` (F31)). No task touches `labs/ts-js`, any `package.json`, `angular.json` or a lockfile. Source reads name the file and function (`grep` first, in `labs/angular/node_modules/@angular/router/fesm2022/_router-chunk.mjs`, `_router_module-chunk.mjs`, `types/router.d.ts`, `types/_router_module-chunk.d.ts`, and `@angular/common/fesm2022/_location-chunk.mjs`, `_common_module-chunk.mjs`). **Documented, never worded as observed:** browser back/forward and scroll restore (C3), the View Transitions animation (C4), the Navigation API integration (C5), server deep-link configuration (C6), network-aware preloading (C7), `nonBlocking` until SEC-M24-06's probe (C9), Angular docs sentences (from `main`, C1). Scratch only under `mktemp -d` outside the repo, deleted at the end. Probes that need output under `ng test` collect it and fail an assertion to print it, in a scratch copy only. Specs assert URLs, event classes (by `instanceof`), cancellation codes, call counts and instance identities, never wall-clock durations (an async guard's `timer(30)` is input); no `console.log`; every bootstrapped root destroyed and its element removed in `finally`; Angular errors asserted by their `NGxxxx` code. A non-spec file (fixtures, exercise sources, `legacy/`) is compiled by `ng build`: no `vi`, no `expect`.

Every internal name of C11 is **marked internal at its first use in each section**. No rationale, roadmap or "why the team chose" claim.

- **First-time-pass rules (from REVIEW-M14 to M23; named so they do not recur):**
  - Factual slips: "which URL", "which event order", "which code", "how many loader calls", "same instance or new" and "which value binds" statements are checked against the recorded runs (F1-F33) before writing; every number in prose is traced to a test, run or read. A navigation that is cancelled **resolves `false`**; only an error **rejects** (F21, F24); a redirect resolves `true` after a second `NavigationStart` (F16).
  - Wording of observation: every "in the lab, X" names a test (`Section N: …`, `Q24.NN …`, `E24.N …`) asserting exactly X; no "not run" for something a test now asserts; no unrecorded run; no unmeasured comparison ("faster", "uses more memory"); a measured comparison names the count.
  - Quotes: a quoted sentence is verbatim from the named file, branch and date; a shortened runtime message carries "(abridged)"; an error code is the one the run gives (`NG04002`, `NG04014`, `NG04016`), attributed to the run or the source, not to the docs; a default is attached to the symbol that declares it (`paramsInheritanceStrategy` and `onSameUrlNavigation` are `RouterConfigOptions`'; `unmatchedInputBehavior` is `ComponentInputBindingOptions`').
  - Header and history: the header lists only what the module teaches and cites; history sentences are dated from the CHANGELOG or typings only.
  - Markers: the marker sits at the **first body mention in the module**, not in a later section or in the question bank; a glossary entry never dates a deprecation the sources do not date.

### Module 25 tasks (PLAN-M25) · common rules
- Inputs for every task: `_meta/modules/M25.md` (its section, question or exercise rows, the budget, "Signal Forms handoff", "Lab decision", "Facts established while planning" F1-F24, "Could not be read" C1-C12, the owner map), STYLE-GUIDE §3-§8, QUALITY-BAR B-E, SYLLABUS §4 (25), the module skeleton, the pilot `modules/17-signals.md` and the finished `modules/23-rxjs-in-depth.md` and `modules/24-routing.md` for Part D depth (read a section, answer or exercise of the same kind before writing; never copy), and `_meta/reviews/REVIEW-M24.md` and `REVIEW-M23.md` § Findings and § Proposed FIX tasks. Re-verify every fact the task uses before writing (lab > package source > official docs/changelog) and record the basis next to the claim; every item under "Could not be read" for the task's section is read or probed first, or the claim is dropped. The facts of M25.md were probed 2026-10-10 on Angular 22.2.1 (`@angular/forms` 22.2.1, `rxjs` 7.8.2, Node 24.21.0, jsdom 30.1.1) under `ng test` and `tsc -p tsconfig.spec.json` in a scratch copy of `labs/angular`; a task re-runs the ones it quotes under `ng test`. Where M25.md says "probe first", the run wins over the plan: write what the run shows and state the difference in the LOG line.
- **What runs and what is documented** (M25.md "Lab decision"): **every runtime claim is asserted by specs in `labs/angular` under `ng test`** (jsdom; zoneless `TestBed`; model-only claims without a component; DOM claims by dispatching `input`/`blur` events on native inputs; template-driven specs await `fixture.whenStable()` (F2); zoneless rendering claims use `autoDetectChanges()` plus `whenStable()`, never `detectChanges()` (F18); async validators under `vi.useFakeTimers()` restored in `finally`; compile-time claims as `// @ts-expect-error` lines checked by `tsc -p tsconfig.spec.json`). No task touches `labs/ts-js`, any `package.json`, `angular.json` or a lockfile. Source reads name the file and function (`grep` first, in `labs/angular/node_modules/@angular/forms/fesm2022/forms.mjs` and `types/forms.d.ts`; `types/signals.d.ts` only for F9). **Documented, never worded as observed:** screen-reader output, IME composition, autofill, the native validation bubble and real focus behavior (C4), Signal Forms (C3, module 26), Angular docs sentences (from `main`, C1), the docs' "pending until complete" line (C5). Scratch only under `mktemp -d` outside the repo, deleted at the end. Probes that need output under `ng test` collect it and fail an assertion to print it, in a scratch copy only. Specs assert values, error maps, statuses, event classes (by `instanceof`), call logs and rendered text, never wall-clock durations (a `timer(300)` in a validator is input); no `console.log`; `console.warn` spies and fake timers restored in `finally`; Angular errors asserted by their `NGxxxxx` code. Every fixture component is standalone with a unique `lab-m25-` selector (the default `ng-component` selector logged `NG0912` collisions in the probe). A non-spec file (exercise sources, `legacy/`) is compiled by `ng build`: no `vi`, no `expect`.
- **Corrections to apply from the plan (they override anything older):** status markers only in the STYLE-GUIDE §3.2 forms at the **first body mention in the module**, plain, with the versions of M25.md "Sections"; **no `[Changed in v22]` marker on `Validators.min`/`max` or the `min`/`max` directives**: the v22 numeric-only change is Signal Forms' rules (F9), stated in §5 and Q25.16 with the CHANGELOG line and the typings, one sentence plus a link to 26; a deprecation is dated only where the typings or CHANGELOG of M25.md date it (C6). **Signal Forms handoff:** no `@angular/forms/signals` import in text or labs; only the sentences M25.md allows (C3), each linking [26](../modules/26-signal-forms.md) file-level. **Name the 07/11/13/16/25 split** (M25.md header): `value` versus `getRawValue()` and nullable versus `nonNullable` typing are 07's; accessible names, `aria-describedby`, WCAG and error summaries are 11's; `[(x)]` desugaring is 13's; `useExisting`, `viewProviders`, `multi` and `forwardRef` are 16's. One sentence plus a link each, never retold. Every internal name of C7 is **marked internal at its first use in each section**. No rationale, roadmap or "why the team chose" claim.
- **Angular code** follows STYLE-GUIDE §7.1 (standalone, `inject()`, signals, signal inputs/outputs, built-in control flow with `track`, v22 file names, `protected`/`readonly`, no `any`, no `as` outside a test of a type error) and RUN.md §10 (at most 4 injected dependencies per class). **Legacy code** lives only under a `legacy/` folder or a `#### Legacy` heading, says what it is, and compiles under `ng build`. Fixtures use the `lab-m25-` prefix (selectors) and `LabM25…` class names.
- **First-time-pass rules (from REVIEW-M14 to M24; named so they do not recur):**
  - Factual slips: "which value", "which error map", "which status", "which event order", "how many calls" and "does it repaint" statements are checked against the recorded runs (F2-F23) before writing; every number in prose is traced to a test, run or read. A status flip repaints a zoneless view and a value-only `setValue` does not (F18); a single never-completing async validator settles and two do not (F14); a group validator's error is on the group (F10).
  - Wording of observation: every "in the lab, X" names a test (`Section N: …`, `Q25.NN …`, `E25.N …`) asserting exactly X; no "not run" for something a test now asserts; no unrecorded run; no unmeasured comparison ("faster", "fewer requests" without a count); a measured comparison names the count.
  - Quotes: a quoted sentence is verbatim from the named file, branch and date; a shortened runtime message carries "(abridged)" (every `NG01xxx` message ends with a docs URL, C12); an error code is the one the run gives (`NG01001`, `NG01002`, `NG01200`, `NG01203`, `NG01354`), attributed to the run or the source, not to the docs; a default is attached to the symbol that declares it (`updateOn` `'change'` is `AbstractControlOptions`'; `callSetDisabledState` `'always'` is the forms modules' config).
  - Header and history: the header lists only what the module teaches and cites; history sentences are dated from the CHANGELOG or typings only.
  - Markers: the marker sits at the **first body mention in the module**, not in a later section or in the question bank; a glossary entry never dates a deprecation the sources do not date.
  - Owner credit: name the owning module correctly in every link sentence (typed-forms typing 07's, accessible errors 11's, two-way binding 13's, banana diagnostic 12's, `multi`/`forwardRef`/`useExisting`/`viewProviders` 16's, `model()` 17's and 19's, the zoneless scheduler 21's, timing operators 22's, `switchMap`/`toSignal`/typeahead 23's, unsaved-changes guard 24's, Signal Forms 26's).
  - Mermaid: every section has a diagram of the type named in M25.md followed by a line starting `What to notice`; quote every label with brackets, colons, `@`, `*`, `[`, `/`, `?`, `#`, parentheses or `=`; parse each diagram with the mermaid parser before finishing.
  - Misconceptions: **every** bullet gives the correction **and a cause clause**; "Once true: … until …" only from a source read in the task.
  - Terms: define at first use with an owner link (M25.md lists the terms per section); run a first-use script over the module before finishing.
  - Code: each `### Code` subsection has numbered steps (QUALITY-BAR B5); a snippet shows what its caption claims, its title matches its code, and it shows every helper and the full template it uses (no hidden helper); sections 1, 2, 3, 4, 7 and 10 have a `#### Legacy` subsection as M25.md says.
  - Mechanism: "How it actually works" answers at least one "why does it behave like that" from a source read, marked "read from the `@angular/forms` 22.2.1 source" with file and function named (each name found by `grep` in the named file), and "read, not run" where no test asserts it.
  - Titles and criteria: a question title counts what the answer gives; Output only where a spec asserts the answer exactly; Output short answers give the result **and the reason**; an exercise criterion's text equals its test title; an alternative offered in an exercise ("or …") passes the same tests or is removed; a marker or placeholder replacement uses only what the typings give.
  - Links: questions linked from their section with their own `[Q25.NN](#q25-NN)`; every link to another module's question is checked against that question's heading before writing (M25.md "Owned elsewhere" names them); links to other modules carry a section or question anchor, not the bare file (26, 27, 29, 33, 36, 41 are planned files: file-level); anchors are generated from the heading text by the GitHub rule (`check-links.mjs` `githubSlug`); `<!-- relink: … -->` only for a target not in the file yet; callouts begin `> [!NOTE]`/`> [!TIP]`/`> [!WARNING]`; a *Coming from the backend* callout is optional (C2) and, if written, reads the Jakarta Validation or Hibernate Validator source first and states **Where the analogy breaks**.
  - Narrative voice: no first person ("we ran", "I found"); "the lab test … shows".
  - Format: a blank line before every `###` heading and before a list that follows a bold label; no doubled commas; no "SYLLABUS" in reader text; exercise Constraints list what is not covered and only asserted behaviors are criteria.
  - SOURCES: every URL and package file read gets a line in `SOURCES.md`, including code-source lines for each exercise and the outputs spec; a script lists URLs in the module not in SOURCES (must print nothing).

- **Marker regions:** a section's region is its marker line plus the six empty `###` headings under it. A question chunk's region is its marker line plus the question anchors and headings up to the next marker (QB-M25-01 also writes the bank intro at its placeholder). ### Module 26 tasks (PLAN-M26) · common rules
- Inputs for every task: `_meta/modules/M26.md` (its section, question or exercise rows, the budget, "Module 25 handoff", "Lab decision", "Facts established while planning" F1-F29, "Could not be read" C1-C12, the owner map), STYLE-GUIDE §3-§8, QUALITY-BAR B-E, SYLLABUS §4 (26), the module skeleton, the pilot `modules/17-signals.md` and the finished `modules/25-forms-reactive-and-template-driven.md` and `modules/24-routing.md` for Part D depth (read a section, answer or exercise of the same kind before writing; never copy), and `_meta/reviews/REVIEW-M25.md` and `REVIEW-M24.md` § Findings and § Proposed FIX tasks. Re-verify every fact the task uses before writing (lab > package source > official docs/changelog) and record the basis next to the claim; every item under "Could not be read" for the task's section is read or probed first, or the claim is dropped. The facts of M26.md were probed 2026-10-11 on Angular 22.2.1 (`@angular/forms` 22.2.1, Node 24.21.0) under `ng test` and `tsc -p tsconfig.spec.json` in a scratch copy of `labs/angular`; a task re-runs the ones it quotes under `ng test`. Where M26.md says "probe first", the run wins over the plan: write what the run shows and state the difference in the LOG line.
- **What runs and what is documented** (M26.md "Lab decision"): **every runtime claim is asserted by specs in `labs/angular` under `ng test`** (jsdom; zoneless `TestBed`; model-only claims inside `TestBed.runInInjectionContext`, because `form()` throws NG0203 elsewhere (F7); DOM claims by dispatching `input`/`blur`/cancelable `submit` events; rendering claims with `autoDetectChanges()` plus `whenStable()`, never `detectChanges()`; **fake timers only in model-only specs**, restored in `finally`, **never with `autoDetectChanges()`** (that probe hung until the 5,000 ms timeout, F12); compile-time claims as `// @ts-expect-error` lines checked by `tsc -p tsconfig.spec.json`, with the TypeScript code recorded). No task touches `labs/ts-js`, any `package.json`, `angular.json` or a lockfile; **no `zod` import** (transitive only, C3). Source reads name the file and function (`grep` first, in `labs/angular/node_modules/@angular/forms/types/{signals,_structure-chunk,signals-compat}.d.ts` and `fesm2022/{signals,_validation_errors-chunk,signals-compat}.mjs`). **Documented, never worded as observed:** screen-reader output and real focus, native pickers, WebMCP (not taught, C5), Angular docs sentences (from `main`, C1), cancellation until a test asserts it (F18), `validateHttp` unless its probe passes (C4). Scratch only under `mktemp -d` outside the repo, deleted at the end. Specs assert values, error kinds, statuses, call logs and rendered text, never wall-clock durations; no `console.log`; Angular errors by their `NGxxxx` code. Every fixture component is standalone with a unique `lab-m26-` selector. A non-spec file (exercise sources, `legacy/`) is compiled by `ng build`: no `vi`, no `expect`.
- **Corrections to apply from the plan (they override anything older):** status markers only in the STYLE-GUIDE §3.2 forms at the **first body mention in the module**, plain, with the versions of M26.md "Sections" (`[Stable since v22.0]` for Signal Forms, `[Added in v22.1]` `isFieldTree`, `[Changed in v22: numbers or null only]` `min`/`max`, `[Changed in v22: touched is an input and blur is reported by a touch output]`, `[Deprecated since v22.0 — use { when }]` for the function overloads, `[Added in v22.0]` `ngNoCva`); no marker on the other 22.0 APIs. **Module 25 handoff:** the v22 `min`/`max` rule, the custom-control contract and interop are taught here; reactive-forms mechanics are 25's and are linked, never retold. **Name the 16/17/25 split:** the injection context is 16's, `linkedSignal`, `resource` and `model()` are 17's, CVA, reactive async validators, error display and `Validators.min` are 25's. Every internal name of C12 is **marked internal at its first use in each section**. No rationale, roadmap or "why the team chose" claim.
- **Angular code** follows STYLE-GUIDE §7.1 (standalone, `inject()`, signals, signal inputs/outputs, built-in control flow with `track`, v22 file names, `protected`/`readonly`, no `any`, no `as` outside a test of a type error) and RUN.md §10 (at most 4 injected dependencies per class). Components import `FormField` (and `FormRoot`) from `@angular/forms/signals`; compat APIs from `@angular/forms/signals/compat`. **Legacy code** lives only under `legacy/` or a `#### Legacy` heading (§5, §8, §9), says what it is, and compiles under `ng build` (§9's v21 block is a `// Partial:` text block). Fixtures use the `lab-m26-` prefix and `LabM26…` class names.
- **First-time-pass rules (from REVIEW-M14 to M25; named so they do not recur):**
  - Factual slips: "which value", "which error kind", "which field holds the error", "pending, valid or invalid", "how many calls" and "does it repaint" statements are checked against the recorded runs (F6-F26) before writing; every number in prose is traced to a test, run or read. Root `errors()` is empty while `errorSummary()` lists descendants (F9); disabled, hidden and readonly fields report no errors (F14); a pending field is neither valid nor invalid (F17); a programmatic `value.set` does not dirty (F8); blur flushes a debounced value (F11).
  - Wording of observation: every "in the lab, X" names a test (`Section N: …`, `Q26.NN …`, `E26.N …`) asserting exactly X; no unrecorded run; no unmeasured comparison; a measured comparison names the count.
  - Quotes: a quoted sentence is verbatim from the named file, branch and date; a shortened runtime message carries "(abridged)"; an error code is the one the run gives (`NG0203`, the TypeScript code of F16), attributed to the run or the source; a default is attached to the symbol that declares it (`ignoreValidators` `'pending'` is `FormSubmitOptions`').
  - Header and history: the header lists only what the module teaches and cites; history sentences are dated from the CHANGELOG, typings tags or the `npm pack` reads of F2/F4 only; CHANGELOG lines above 22.2.1 are never cited as shipped (C1).
  - Markers: at the **first body mention in the module**, not in a later section or in the question bank; a glossary entry never dates what the sources do not date.
  - Owner credit: name the owning module correctly in every link sentence (injection context 16's, `linkedSignal`/`resource`/`model()` 17's, `model()` versus `input()` 19's, the zoneless scheduler 21's, timing operators 22's, `rxResource` and the typeahead 23's, CVA/reactive validators/error display/`Validators.min` 25's, accessibility 11's, two-way binding 13's, HTTP 27's, testing 29's).
  - Mermaid: every section has a diagram of the type named in M26.md followed by a line starting `What to notice`; quote every label with brackets, colons, `@`, `*`, `[`, `/`, `?`, `#`, parentheses or `=`; parse each diagram with the mermaid parser before finishing.
  - Misconceptions: **every** bullet gives the correction **and a cause clause**; "Once true: … until …" only from a source read in the task.
  - Terms: define at first use with an owner link (M26.md lists the terms per section); run a first-use script over the module before finishing.
  - Code: each `### Code` subsection has numbered steps (QUALITY-BAR B5); a snippet shows what its caption claims and every helper and the full template it uses; sections 5, 8 and 9 have a `#### Legacy` subsection as M26.md says.
  - Mechanism: "How it actually works" answers at least one "why does it behave like that" from a source read, marked "read from the `@angular/forms` 22.2.1 source" with file and function named (each name found by `grep` in the named file), and "read, not run" where no test asserts it.
  - Titles and criteria: a question title counts what the answer gives; Output only where a spec asserts the answer exactly; Output short answers give the result **and the reason**; an exercise criterion's text equals its test title; an alternative offered in an exercise passes the same tests or is removed.
  - Links: questions linked from their section with their own `[Q26.NN](#q26-NN)`; every link to another module's question is checked against that question's heading before writing; links to other modules carry a section or question anchor (27, 28, 29, 36 are planned files: file-level); anchors follow `check-links.mjs` `githubSlug`; `<!-- relink: … -->` only for a target not in the file yet; callouts begin `> [!NOTE]`/`> [!TIP]`/`> [!WARNING]`; a *Coming from the backend* callout is optional (C2) and, if written, reads the Jakarta Validation or Hibernate Validator source first and states **Where the analogy breaks**.
  - Narrative voice: no first person; "the lab test … shows".
  - Format: a blank line before every `###` heading and before a list that follows a bold label; no doubled commas; no "SYLLABUS" in reader text; exercise Constraints list what is not covered and only asserted behaviors are criteria.
  - SOURCES: every URL and package file read gets a line in `SOURCES.md`, including code-source lines for each exercise and the outputs spec; a script lists URLs in the module not in SOURCES (must print nothing).
  - Repeats: tell each mechanism once and link it afterwards; the model sync (§2), the skip rule for disabled/hidden/readonly (§5), the async resource mapping (§6), the submit protocol (§7) and the v21-to-v22 table (§9) are the likeliest to be retold in questions and exercises, and those link the section.
- **Marker regions:** a section's region is its marker line plus the six empty `###` headings under it. A question chunk's region is its marker line plus the question anchors and headings up to the next marker (QB-M26-01 also writes the bank intro at its placeholder). An exercise's region is its marker line, its `<a id>` and its heading (EX-M26-01 also writes the exercise intro; SEC-M26-01 writes the verification paragraph at its placeholder). CLOSE-M26's marker is in `## Summary`; the placeholders for Short on time, Check your understanding and Connections name CLOSE-M26, and the header's Labs line carries a relink comment for CLOSE-M26.
- **Prose budget** (deltas over the module count measured just before the task; M26.md "Budget"): skeleton 1,695 measured 2026-10-11 by `node labs/tools/module-stats.mjs` and the QUALITY-BAR python one-liner (equal). **Per-chunk caps, summing to the CLOSE limit:** SEC-M26-01..09 = 900 / 800 / 800 / 900 / 850 / 850 / 850 / 850 / 900 (7,700); EX-M26-01 = 560 (intro included), EX-M26-02..05 = 520 each (2,640); QB-M26-01..04 = 1,130 each, QB-M26-05..06 = 904 each (6,328; QB-M26-01 includes the bank intro of at most 40 words); CLOSE-M26 = 800. 1,695 + 7,700 + 2,640 + 6,328 + 800 = 19,163. **CLOSE at most 19,170 words; REVIEW ceiling 20,070.** Each task measures before and after with both counters, puts both counts in its LOG line, and cuts before finishing if more than 5% over its delta (repeats first; never a diagram, a trap's cause or a "because"). A 2xx parse failure is an `HttpErrorResponse` with status 200 (F16); status 0 covers network, timeout and the `NG02824` refusal (F16, F18, F25); the testing backend does not simulate `timeout` (F18); a child `provideHttpClient` is a separate client (F9); a params change resets `httpResource`'s value (F26).
  - Wording of observation: every "in the lab, X" names a test (`Section N: …`, `Q27.NN …`, `E27.N …`) asserting exactly X; no unrecorded run; no unmeasured comparison; a measured comparison names the count.
  - Quotes: a quoted sentence is verbatim from the named file, branch and date; a shortened runtime message carries "(abridged)"; an error code is the one the run gives (`NG02824`, `NG0203`), attributed to the run or the source; a default is attached to the symbol that declares it (`XSRF-TOKEN`/`X-XSRF-TOKEN` are the XSRF defaults, F24).
  - Header and history: the header lists only what the module teaches and cites; history sentences are dated from the CHANGELOG, typings tags or the `npm pack` read of F4 only; CHANGELOG lines above 22.2.1 are never cited as shipped (C1).
  - Markers: at the **first body mention in the module**, not in a later section or in the question bank; a glossary entry never dates what the sources do not date.
  - Owner credit: name the owning module correctly in every link sentence (`AbortController` 04's, Zod 07's, the platform, CORS and cookies 09's, module packaging 15's, multi providers and environment injectors 16's, `resource` 17's, `PendingTasks` 21's, cold Observables 22's, operators, cancellation, retry and `shareReplay` 23's, resolvers 24's, `validateHttp` 26's, state 28's, testing strategy 29's, SSR 32's, security depth 33's, API contracts 41's, authentication 42's).
  - Mermaid: every section has a diagram of the type named in M27.md followed by a line starting `What to notice`; quote every label with brackets, colons, `@`, `*`, `[`, `/`, `?`, `#`, parentheses or `=`; parse each diagram with the mermaid parser before finishing.
  - Misconceptions: **every** bullet gives the correction **and a cause clause**; "Once true: … until …" only from a source read in the task.
  - Terms: define at first use with an owner link (M27.md lists the terms per section); run a first-use script over the module before finishing.
  - Code: each `### Code` subsection has numbered steps (QUALITY-BAR B5); a snippet shows what its caption claims and every helper and the full template it uses; sections 2, 4, 9 and 11 have a `#### Legacy` subsection as M27.md says.
  - Mechanism: "How it actually works" answers at least one "why does it behave like that" from a source read, marked "read from the `@angular/common` 22.2.1 source" with file and function named (each name found by `grep` in the named file), and "read, not run" where no test asserts it.
  - Titles and criteria: a question title counts what the answer gives; Output only where a spec asserts the answer exactly; Output short answers give the result **and the reason**; an exercise criterion's text equals its test title; an alternative offered in an exercise passes the same tests or is removed.
  - Links: questions linked from their section with their own `[Q27.NN](#q27-NN)`; every link to another module's question is checked against that question's heading before writing; links to other modules carry a section or question anchor (28, 29, 32, 33, 37, 41, 42, 43 are planned files: file-level); anchors follow `check-links.mjs` `githubSlug`; `<!-- relink: … -->` only for a target not in the file yet; callouts begin `> [!NOTE]`/`> [!TIP]`/`> [!WARNING]`; the *Framework vs platform* callout is required in §1; a *Coming from the backend* callout is optional (C2) and, if written, reads the Spring Framework 7 reference first and states **Where the analogy breaks**.
  - Narrative voice: no first person; "the lab test … shows".
  - Format: a blank line before every `###` heading and before a list that follows a bold label; no doubled commas; no "SYLLABUS" in reader text; exercise Constraints list what is not covered and only asserted behaviors are criteria.
  - SOURCES: every URL and package file read gets a line in `SOURCES.md`, including code-source lines for each exercise and the outputs spec; a script lists URLs in the module not in SOURCES (must print nothing).
  - Repeats: tell each mechanism once and link it afterwards; the backend matrix (§2), the chain order (§4), the error-shape table (§5), abort and `timeout` (§6), the refresh queue (§7), the XSRF gates (§8) and the `httpResource` lifecycle (§10) are the likeliest to be retold in questions and exercises, and those link the section.
- **Marker regions:** a section's region is its marker line plus the six empty `###` headings under it. A question chunk's region is its marker line plus the question anchors and headings up to the next marker (QB-M27-01 also writes the bank intro at its placeholder). An exercise's region is its marker line, its `<a id>` and its heading (EX-M27-01 also writes the exercise intro; SEC-M27-01 writes the verification paragraph at its placeholder). CLOSE-M27's marker is in `## Summary`; the placeholders for Short on time, Check your understanding and Connections name CLOSE-M27, and the header's Labs line carries a relink comment for CLOSE-M27.
- **Prose budget** (deltas over the module count measured just before the task; M27.md "Budget"): skeleton 1,973 measured 2026-10-11 by `node labs/tools/module-stats.mjs` and the QUALITY-BAR python one-liner (equal). **Per-chunk caps, summing to the CLOSE limit:** SEC-M27-01..11 = 900 / 800 / 800 / 850 / 850 / 850 / 800 / 700 / 700 / 850 / 750 (8,850); EX-M27-01 = 560 (intro included), EX-M27-02..06 = 520 each (3,160); QB-M27-01..06 = 1,130 each, QB-M27-07 = 904 (7,684; QB-M27-01 includes the bank intro of at most 40 words); CLOSE-M27 = 800. 1,973 + 8,850 + 3,160 + 7,684 + 800 = 22,467. **CLOSE at most 22,470 words; REVIEW ceiling 23,370.** Each task measures before and after with both counters, puts both counts in its LOG line, and cuts before finishing if more than 5% over its delta (repeats first; never a diagram, a trap's cause or a "because"). Answer parts average at most 226 words per QB chunk, none above 290.

Never touch another task's marker. Labs: only the files M27.md "Lab files" assigns to the task, under `labs/angular/src/app/modules/27-http-client/` (nothing under `labs/ts-js`; other modules' lab files read-only). No test needs the internet. Throwaway probes live only in a scratch directory and are deleted before the task ends.

- **Prose budget** (deltas over the module count measured just before the task; M29.md "Budget"): skeleton 2,008 measured 2026-10-13 by `node labs/tools/module-stats.mjs` and the QUALITY-BAR python one-liner (equal). **Per-chunk caps, summing to the CLOSE limit:** SEC-M29-01..12 = 900 / 850 / 700 / 750 / 850 / 800 / 750 / 700 / 850 / 800 / 750 / 600 (9,300); EX-M29-01 = 560 (intro included), EX-M29-02..06 = 520 each (3,160); QB-M29-01..06 = 1,130 each, QB-M29-07 = 904 (7,684; QB-M29-01 includes the bank intro of at most 40 words); CLOSE-M29 = 800. 2,008 + 9,300 + 3,160 + 7,684 + 800 = 22,952. **CLOSE at most 22,952 words; REVIEW ceiling 23,852.** Each task measures before and after with both counters, puts both counts in its LOG line, and cuts before finishing if more than 5% over its delta (repeats first; never a diagram, a trap's cause or a "because"). Answer parts average at most 226 words per QB chunk, none above 290.
- Module file: replace only the task's own `<!-- TASK: <ID> -->` region, at the end of the task, in a single edit. `<!-- PLACEHOLDER: … -->` lines are replaced by the task named in them. Never touch another task's marker. Labs: only the files M29.md "Lab files" assigns to the task, under `labs/angular/src/app/modules/29-testing-angular/` (other modules' lab files read-only). Throwaway files live only in the scratchpad and are deleted before the task ends.
- **Marker regions:** a section's region is its marker line plus the six empty `###` headings under it. A question chunk's region is its marker line plus the question anchors and headings up to the next marker (QB-M29-01 also writes the bank intro at its placeholder). An exercise's region is its marker line, its `<a id>` and its heading (EX-M29-01 also writes the exercise intro; SEC-M29-01 writes the verification paragraph at its placeholder). CLOSE-M29's marker is in `## Summary`; the placeholders for Short on time, Applies to, Check your understanding and Connections name CLOSE-M29, and the header's Labs line carries a relink comment for CLOSE-M29.
- Every task adds its sources under `## Module 29 · Testing Angular` in `SOURCES.md` (after the last module section present; package reads as `<pkg>@<version>, <file>, read <date>`) and its inline-defined terms under `## Module 29` in `_meta/GLOSSARY-TERMS.md`.
- Acceptance for every task: the module's lab tests pass (`labs/angular`: `npx ng test --watch=false --include='src/app/modules/29-testing-angular/**/*.spec.ts'` and `npx tsc -p tsconfig.spec.json --noEmit`, plus `npx ng build` when a non-spec file changed); module 28's lab tests still pass; `node labs/tools/check-snippets.mjs . 29` and `node labs/tools/check-links.mjs --planned` exit 0; every URL in the module is in SOURCES.md; only the declared files are new or changed (`git status --short`); the task's marker is gone; no scratch or probe file is left behind; the LOG line gives the part's and the module's prose count (and the HOUSE-16 mode for SEC-M29-01, -11 and EX-M29-05).

- **First-time-pass rules (from REVIEW-M14 to M34; named so they do not recur):** every recorded class list, event order, animation kind, pseudo-element name, timing value, error code, console message and layout count is checked against the run before writing; every "in the lab, X" names a test (`Section N: …`, `Q35.NN …`, or the criterion title) asserting exactly X; **no throwaway observation in reader text** (REVIEW-M32 T-3): anything not asserted by a committed test is "read, not run" with its package, version, file and function; quotes verbatim from the named file, version or URL and date, a shortened message carries "(abridged)"; owner credit is named correctly in every link sentence; every section has its Mermaid diagram of the type M35.md names followed by a line starting `What to notice`, parsed with the mermaid parser; **every Misconceptions bullet gives the correction and a cause clause** (M35.md names each cause); **terms defined at first use** (M35.md lists them per section), checked by a first-use script; **internal names marked internal at first use in each section** (C8); each `### Code` has numbered steps; each mechanism answers one "why" from a source read named with package, version, file and function; **status markers at first body mention** (C5); **links into written modules carry anchors** (M35.md names them; only planned modules stay file-level); Output short answers give the result and its reason; at least two answered follow-ups per answer (script per chunk); an exercise criterion's text equals its test title and the alternative runs the same criteria; every `<details>` closed with no `###` inside; a blank line before every `###` and before a list after a bold label; no "SYLLABUS", "probe" or "planner" in reader text; exercise Constraints list what is not covered; every URL, package file and registry read gets a SOURCES line (a script lists module URLs missing from SOURCES and must print nothing).
- **Prose budget** (deltas over the module count measured just before the task; M35.md "Budget"): skeleton 1,808 measured 2026-10-16 by `node labs/tools/module-stats.mjs` and the QUALITY-BAR python one-liner (equal). Tarballs are `npm pack`ed into the job scratchpad, read and deleted before the task ends; nothing is installed.

- Every task adds its sources under `## Module 40 · Framework comparisons` in `SOURCES.md` (after the last module section present; package reads as `<pkg>@<version>, <file>, <function>, read <date>`; docs as `<repo> <path>, read <date>` or the URL with the date; registry reads as `npm view <pkg> <fields>, read <date>` or `api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/last-week/<pkg>, week <start> to <end>, read <date>`) and its inline-defined terms under `## Module 40` in `_meta/GLOSSARY-TERMS.md`.

- **Lab rules:** Angular specs only under `labs/angular/src/app/modules/41-fullstack-api-contracts/` (`concepts/`, `outputs/`, `exercise-N-*/`), using `HttpTestingController` or the real fetch backend with `vi.stubGlobal('fetch', …)` returning prepared `Response` objects (and `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` after each test), as 27's specs do; plain TypeScript tests only under `labs/ts-js/src/modules/41-fullstack-api-contracts/` and the Output test under `labs/ts-js/src/outputs/41-fullstack-api-contracts/` (STYLE-GUIDE §7.3, `captureLogs` from `src/outputs/capture.ts`, read-only); **no test calls `git`, `npm` or the network, reads the clock (`Date.now()`, `new Date()` without an argument) or depends on the machine's time zone** (every formatting call passes `timeZone`); no file under `labs/e2e`; no `labs/spring-backend/` (C19).
- **Shared files (C20):** no task edits `package.json`, a lockfile, a tsconfig, `vitest.config.ts`, `angular.json`, `src/outputs/capture.ts`, VERSIONS.md or another module's folder or file. Read-only to later tasks once created: labs/angular `concepts/problem-details.ts` (SEC-M41-05), `concepts/page-params.ts` (SEC-M41-06), `concepts/json-pointer.ts` (SEC-M41-07); labs/ts-js `concepts/wire-codecs.ts` (SEC-M41-09).

Java snippets illustrative under the banner; `proxy.conf.json`, YAML and OpenAPI JSON fences are non-TS fences; generated code shown is Partial (M41.md "Lab decision").
- **First-time-pass rules (from REVIEW-M14 to M39; named so they do not recur):** every recorded version, default, property, class name, message and header is checked against the named file or dated read before writing; every "in the lab, X" names a test (`Section N: …`, `Q41.NN …`, or the criterion title) asserting exactly X; **no throwaway observation in reader text**: anything not asserted by a committed test is "read, not run" with its artifact, version, file and class, or a dated docs, RFC or registry read; quotes verbatim from the named file, version or URL and date, a shortened quote carries "(abridged)"; owner credit is named correctly in every link sentence; every section has its Mermaid diagram of the type M41.md names followed by a line starting `What to notice`, parsed with the mermaid parser; **every Misconceptions bullet gives the correction and a cause clause** (M41.md names each cause); **terms defined at first use** (M41.md lists them per section), checked by a first-use script; **internal names marked internal at first use in each section** (C17); each `### Code` has numbered steps; each mechanism answers one "why" from a source read; the Output short answer gives the result and its reason, in the same words as the full explanation; **every answer and every exercise has at least two answered follow-ups**; **every question and exercise is linked from the body** ("Drilled in …" at the end of the section's Misconceptions, "practised in …" where an exercise applies the section); no process words ("probe", "planner") and no task ID in reader text; links into written modules carry anchors.

Answer parts average at most 105 words per QB chunk, none above 140.

Forward links to questions and exercises not written yet are plain text with a `<!-- relink: #q41-NN -->` (or `#ex41-N`) comment; the QB or EX task that writes the target restores them, and CLOSE checks none remain.

Caps: SEC-M44-01..10 = 460 / 340 / 400 / 360 / 340 / 380 / 340 / 340 / 320 / 400 (3,680); EX-M44-01 = 400 (intro included), EX-M44-02 = 370, EX-M44-03 = 370 (1,140); QB-M44-01 = 880 (intro included), QB-M44-02 = 735, QB-M44-03 = 630 (2,245); CLOSE-M44 = 440. 1,793 + 3,680 + 1,140 + 2,245 + 440 = 9,298. **CLOSE at most 9,298 words; REVIEW ceiling 9,850; hard cap 10,000.** Each task measures before and after with both counters, puts both in its LOG line, and cuts before finishing if more than 5% over its delta (repeats first; never a "Must state" fact, a diagram, a cause, a follow-up's reason or a "because"); if the facts still do not fit, the task stops and reports instead (M44.md lesson 22). Answer parts average at most 105 words per QB chunk, none above 145.
- Module file: replace only the task's own `<!-- TASK: <ID> -->` region, at the end of the task, in a single edit; `<!-- PLACEHOLDER: … -->` lines are replaced by the task named in them; never touch another task's marker. **Marker regions:** a section's region is its marker line plus the six empty `###` headings under it (SEC-M44-01 also writes the verification paragraph at its placeholder before §1); a question chunk's region is its marker line plus the anchors and headings up to the next marker (QB-M44-01 also writes the bank intro at its placeholder); an exercise's region is its marker line, its `<a id>` and its heading (EX-M44-01 also writes the exercise intro at its placeholder). CLOSE-M44's marker is in `## Summary`; the placeholders for Applies to, Short on time, Check your understanding and Connections name CLOSE-M44, and the header's Labs line carries a relink comment for CLOSE-M44. Forward links to questions and exercises not written yet are plain text with a `<!-- relink: #q44-NN -->` (or `#ex44-N`) comment; the QB or EX task that writes the target restores them, and CLOSE checks none remain.
- **Acceptance for every task:** when a `labs/ts-js` file changed: from `labs/ts-js` (Node 24), `npx vitest run src/modules/44-fullstack-delivery-and-operations src/outputs/44-fullstack-delivery-and-operations` and `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0; when a `labs/angular` file changed: from `labs/angular`, `npx ng test --watch=false --include='src/app/modules/44-fullstack-delivery-and-operations/**/*.spec.ts'` and `npx tsc -p tsconfig.spec.json --noEmit` exit 0 (and `npx ng build` when non-spec code was added); from the guide root, `node labs/tools/check-snippets.mjs . 44` and `node labs/tools/check-links.mjs --planned` exit 0; `node labs/tools/module-stats.mjs` and the QUALITY-BAR python one-liner give the module's prose (both in the LOG line); every URL in the module is in SOURCES.md; only the declared files are new or changed (`git status --short`; `node_modules/` and `dist/` are ignored); the task's marker is gone; no scratch, tarball or temporary file left; the LOG line gives both prose counts and the "Must state" facts written. The main session runs every check serially; writers report readiness.

Read-only to later tasks once created: every `concepts/*.ts` model (`prefix-cache.ts`, `feed-pager.ts`, `grid-query.ts`, `wizard.ts`, `aggregator.ts`, `unread.ts`, `presence.ts`, `transfer.ts`).

API contracts are `http` or `text` fences whose first line is `# Illustrative contract, not a lab API`; a contract that shows an idempotent POST shows `Idempotency-Key` with a quoted String value, and one that shows a conditional draft save shows `If-Match` (lesson 27). ARIA markup is an `html` fence whose first line is `<!-- Partial: illustrative markup after the APG <pattern> pattern, not a lab file -->`. No Java, no YAML. Mermaid only in STYLE-GUIDE §11's types (C14).
- **First-time-pass rules (from REVIEW-M14 to M45; named so they do not recur):** every recorded number, version, criterion and quote is checked against the named file or dated read before writing; every "in the lab, X" names a test (`Section N: …`, `Q46.NN …`, or the criterion title) asserting exactly X; **no throwaway observation in reader text**: anything not asserted by a committed test is "read, not run" with its artifact and version or a dated page; quotes verbatim with their subject ("the resource SHOULD …"), a shortened quote carries "(abridged)"; owner credit is named correctly in every link sentence; every section has its Mermaid diagram of the type M46.md names followed by a line starting `What to notice` (checked by eye against a diagram of the same type in module 45 or 43, C14); **every case section carries §1's template parts in order** (assumed numbers, diagram, contract, state, failure modes, kernel); **every Misconceptions bullet gives a correction that states the true belief and a cause clause that says why the myth is natural** (M46.md writes each; reword, never drop; REVIEW-M45 T-2); **terms defined at first use** (M46.md lists them per section); **each `### Code` has numbered steps, and every step says what the code does and why that way, and holds for every branch the excerpt shows** (REVIEW-M45 F-3, N-6); **one byte unit** (plain byte counts, or KB = 1,000 as §1 states; REVIEW-M45 T-1); **a statement about one layer, object or branch is not stated for all** (REVIEW-M45 F-2, F-4); **a source is cited only for what it says** (REVIEW-M45 F-5); each mechanism answers one "why" from a source read or an owner linked; **direction facts (M46.md lesson 16's list) are re-read at their source just before the sentence is written, and the task's LOG line names the page and paragraph for each**; **Full explanations teach before they route and end on teaching, not a bare link** (REVIEW-M44 T-1, REVIEW-M45 T-3); the Output short answer gives the result and its reason, in the same words as the full explanation; **every answer and every exercise has at least two answered follow-ups, and every follow-up answer and every trap gives its reason** (a follow-up that cannot carry its reason is replaced, not shortened); **every "Must state" fact of the task's section appears in reader text; a fact that cannot fit is moved, with its F-number, to a named question or exercise in M46.md "Corrections found while writing", never dropped**; **every handoff line M46.md assigns to the task is honored**; every question and exercise is linked from the body ("Drilled in …" at the end of the section's Misconceptions, "practised in …" where an exercise applies the section); **references to other sections or modules are links, not plain text**; no process words ("probe", "planner") and no task ID in reader text; links into written modules carry anchors; links in `_meta/` files use `../../modules/<file>#slug`.
